ready1_open_rewrite.raw_question_text: In rectangle $ABCD$, $AB=4$, $BC=5$, P is a moving point on ray $BC$, draw $PE\perp AP$, $PE$ intersects ray $DC$ at point E, ray $AE$ intersects ray $BC$ at point F, let $BP=x$, $CF=y$. When $\sin\angle APB=\frac{4}{5}$, what is the length of $CE$?
ready1_open_rewrite.raw_answer_text:
\textbf{Solution:} In the right triangle $Rt\triangle APB$, where $AB=4$ and $\sin\angle APB=\frac{4}{5}$,
\[
\therefore \sin\angle APB=\frac{AB}{AP}=\frac{4}{5}, \text{ thus } \frac{4}{AP}=\frac{4}{5},
\]
\[
\therefore AP=5,
\]
\[
\therefore PB=\sqrt{AP^2-AB^2}=3,
\]
\[
\therefore PC=BC-PB=5-3=2,
\]
\[
\because PE\perp AP,
\]
\[
\therefore \angle CPE+\angle APB=90^\circ,
\]
\[
\because \angle BAP+\angle APB=90^\circ,
\]
\[
\therefore \angle CPE=\angle BAP,
\]
\[
\because \angle ECP=\angle B=90^\circ,
\]
\[
\therefore \triangle PCE\sim \triangle ABP,
\]
\[
\therefore \frac{CE}{BP}=\frac{PC}{AB},
\]
\[
\therefore CE=\frac{BP\cdot PC}{AB}=\frac{3\times 2}{4}=\boxed{\frac{3}{2}}
\]

raw_record.original_question: In rectangle $ABCD$, $AB=4$, $BC=5$. Point $P$ is on ray $BC$. Draw $PE\perp AP$; $PE$ intersects ray $DC$ at point $E$, and ray $AE$ intersects ray $BC$ at point $F$. Let $BP=x$ and $CF=y$. When $\sin\angle APB=\frac{4}{5}$, what is the length of $CE$?
raw_record.answer:
Solution: In the right triangle $Rt\triangle APB$, where $AB=4$ and $\sin\angle APB=\frac{4}{5}$,
\[
\therefore \sin\angle APB=\frac{AB}{AP}=\frac{4}{5}, \text{ thus } \frac{4}{AP}=\frac{4}{5},
\]
\[
\therefore AP=5,
\]
\[
\therefore PB=\sqrt{AP^2-AB^2}=3,
\]
\[
\therefore PC=BC-PB=5-3=2,
\]
\[
\because PE\perp AP,
\]
\[
\therefore \angle CPE+\angle APB=90^\circ,
\]
\[
\because \angle BAP+\angle APB=90^\circ,
\]
\[
\therefore \angle CPE=\angle BAP,
\]
\[
\because \angle ECP=\angle B=90^\circ,
\]
\[
\therefore \triangle PCE\sim \triangle ABP,
\]
\[
\therefore \frac{CE}{BP}=\frac{PC}{AB},
\]
\[
\therefore CE=\frac{BP\cdot PC}{AB}=\frac{3\times 2}{4}=\boxed{\frac{3}{2}}
\]
raw_record.final_cot: Image description: On the left side of the figure is rectangle ABCD, with A at the upper left, B at the lower left, C at the lower right, and D at the upper right; P is located on the bottom side BC and between B and C; E is located on the right vertical side DC; AP, PE, and AE are connected, and after AE is extended, it intersects the extension line of BC at F. On the right side there is also a backup rectangle diagram with only ABCD labeled. Reasoning: Because ABCD is a rectangle, AB is perpendicular to BC, and P is on BC, therefore triangle APB is right-angled at B. It is known that AB=4, sin∠APB=4/5. In right triangle APB, sin∠APB=AB/AP, so 4/AP=4/5, obtaining AP=5. By the Pythagorean theorem, BP=sqrt(5^2-4^2)=3. Also BC=5, and at this time P is between B and C, so PC=BC-BP=5-3=2. From the figure and conditions, PE is perpendicular to AP; E is on the vertical DC, and P and C are on the horizontal BC, so EC is perpendicular to PC, and triangle PCE is right-angled at C. Because PE is perpendicular to AP, and PB and PC are collinear in opposite directions, it can be obtained that ∠CPE+∠APB=90°; also in triangle APB, ∠BAP+∠APB=90°, so ∠CPE=∠BAP. Together with ∠ECP=∠ABP=90°, therefore triangle PCE is similar to triangle ABP. The corresponding sides are CE↔BP and PC↔AB, so CE/BP=PC/AB, hence CE=BP·PC/AB=3×2/4=3/2.
